report.question_or_target: What algorithm or protocol converts N findings into a causal hierarchy (root cause, contributing factor, symptom) rather than a flat list, how is a proposed parent-child edge falsified, and what does it do with a finding that has two independent causes?
report.answer_summary: Use evidence-gated causal DAG/hypergraph extraction, not nearest-parent clustering: normalize scoped findings without causalizing them, generate declare/absent candidates from receipt rows plus Path.is_file, preregister a branch-isolated set() falsifier (drop-row and materialize-file on a temp tree), require a resolved source measurement plus a mechanically different verifier, encode OR of AND-pairs for independent sufficient causes, classify roles only after edge adjudication, and leave unsupported nodes UNATTRIBUTED. direct_answer.algorithm_or_protocol: Evidence-Gated Causal DAG with Minimal Sufficient Cause Sets (EGCD-MSC): candidate generation from typed observations, intervention-aware edge adjudication, explicit source/verifier signal records, post-graph role classification.
direct_answer.edge_falsification: Refute A->B by a sensitive, branch-isolated intervention: drop the declaring receipt row or materialize the named path in a temp tree and re-run unit_manifest.derive. An inert test is INCONCLUSIVE; first-red movement or isolated-green is the observation.
direct_answer.two_independent_causes: Represent two sufficient causes as two AND-pairs under an OR gate (NASA cut-set form). Do not choose one parent for tree shape. Measured: BLD-0016, CC-0010, and TST-0350 are each independently sufficient for CHECK-RED.
direct_answer.unknown_cause: Keep the finding as UNATTRIBUTED with no incoming accepted edge. Forced lexical-nearest attachment is a known-bad mutant and must exit nonzero.
